When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. ## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

===HEAD OF SCRIPT===
# daily-backup.ps1 — KeystoneOS durability automation (macOS port, 2026-08-05)
# Runs daily at 00:30 via launchd agent "com.keystone.dailybackup".
# Windows original preserved at daily-backup.ps1.win-orig.
#
# Jobs:
#   1. Git-sync the memory repos (auto-commit + push).
#   2. Snapshot non-git stores to the cloud targets (rsync, ADDITIVE - no delete).
#   3. Manifest-driven coverage. backup-manifest.json is the single authority.
#
# COVERAGE MODEL — three states, all covered (each gap was a real failure):
#   tracked + committed + pushed  -> GitHub
#   untracked or ignored          -> SSD (captureOrphans)
#   tracked + modified            -> SSD (captureWorkingTree)
# DEFAULT-DENY: a DEV directory absent from the manifest raises an error.
# Never reintroduce repo-detection as a coverage test.

param([switch]$DryRun)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$U = $HOME
$DevRoot = "$U/DEV"                       # was Desktop\DEV on Windows
$LogDir = "$U/.claude/scripts/logs"
$LogFile = "$LogDir/daily-backup.log"
$StateFile = "$LogDir/backup-state.json"
$ErrorsLog = "$U/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
$Errors = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
# Per-copy wall-clock ceiling for Invoke-Rsync's watchdog. Generous: the largest healthy
# snapshot here finishes in seconds, so anything near this is wedged, not busy.
$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900
$Results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $LogDir | Out-Null

function Log($msg) {
    $line = "{0} {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'), $msg
    Add-Content -Path $LogFile -Value $line
    Write-Output $line
}

function Sync-Repo($path, $branch) {
    $name = Split-Path $path -Leaf
    if ($path -eq "$U/.claude") { $name = 'dotclaude' }
    if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $path '.git'))) { $Errors.Add("repo-missing:$name"); return }
    Push-Location $path
    try {
        git fetch origin 2>&1 | Out-Null
        $counts = git rev-list --left-right --count "origin/$branch...HEAD" 2>$null
        $behind = 0; $ahead = 0
        if ($counts) { $p = $counts -split '\s+'; $behind = [int]$p[0]; $ahead = [int]$p[1] }
        $dirty = (git status --porcelain | Measure-Object).Count

        if ($behind -gt 0 -and ($ahead -gt 0 -or $dirty -gt 0)) {
            # Diverged with local changes: never merge blindly from automation.
            $Errors.Add("repo-diverged:$name")
            Log "REPO $name : DIVERGED (behind=$behind ahead=$ahead dirty=$dirty) - manual reconcile needed"
            return
        }
        if ($behind -gt 0) {
            if (-not $DryRun) { git pull --ff-only origin $branch 2>&1 | Out-Null }
            Log "REPO $name : $(if ($DryRun) { '[dry-run] would fast-forward' } else { 'fast-forwarded' }) $behind commit(s)"
===PARAMS===

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/CreateSkill

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/CreateSkill/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


## 🚨 MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the CreateSkill skill to ACTION"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **CreateSkill** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# CreateSkill

Complete skill development lifecycle: **structure** (create, validate, canonicalize) + **effectiveness** (test, improve, optimize triggers). Structural workflows ensure skills follow LifeOS conventions. Effectiveness workflows — inspired by Anthropic's skill-creator — ensure skills actually work and trigger reliably.

## Enforcement

Handrolling skill files — writing `SKILL.md` or `Workflows/`, `Tools/`, `References/` by hand — is forbidden by `skills/CLAUDE.md`. Spawn this skill first and let it orchestrate. Reading these workflows and performing the steps yourself is the exact anti-pattern the rule exists to prevent.

This skill is the **single home** for skill authoring here. `write-a-skill` is a pointer to it; `superpowers:writing-skills` is a third-party plugin skill and is not the authority in this workspace. (Consolidated 2026-08-15.)

*This text used to live in the frontmatter `description`. Descriptions load into every session's system prompt, so enforcement prose belongs in the body — the description now carries only what is needed to trigger.*

## Authoritative Source

**Before creating ANY skill, READ:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md`

**Canonical example to follow:** any well-formed public skill in `~/.claude/skills/` (e.g. `Research/SKILL.md`, `Daemon/SKILL.md`, `CreateSkill/SKILL.md` itself).

## Naming Convention — Public vs Private

**Skill name encodes its public/private status. There are exactly two valid forms.**

| Skill type | Directory format | Example | Allowed content |
|------------|------------------|---------|-----------------|
| **Public** | `TitleCase` | `Blogging`, `Daemon`, `CreateSkill` | Templated, safe, generic, ready for public release |
| **Private** | `_ALLCAPS` (underscore prefix, all uppercase) | `<your-release-skill>`, `_INBOX`, `_BROADCAST`, `_DOTFILES` | Anything personal, sensitive, identity-bound, customer-bound, or environment-specific |

**The leading underscore is the public-release boundary.** Release tooling skips `_*` skills entirely — they never leave `~/.claude`. Public skills (no underscore) are mirrored into the LifeOS public release and MUST contain only generic, templated content.

**Sub-file naming (both public and private skills):**

| Component | Format | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Workflow files | `TitleCase.md` | `Create.md`, `UpdateDaemonInfo.md` |
| Reference docs | `TitleCase.md` | `ProsodyGuide.md`, `ApiReference.md` |
| Tool files | `TitleCase.ts` | `ManageServer.ts` |
| Help files | `TitleCase.help.md` | `ManageServer.help.md` |

**Wrong (NEVER use):**
- Skill dirs: `createskill`, `create-skill`, `CREATE_SKILL` (no underscore + caps for public; no kebab/snake for private)
- Files: `create.md`, `update-info.md`, `SYNC_REPO.md`

### Choosing public vs private — the decision rule

Ask: **"Could this skill be dropped, as-is, into a stranger's `~/.claude/skills/` and just work?"**

- **Yes** → public skill (`TitleCase`). Body must be generic; user-specific config layers in via `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/`.
- **No, because it references my identity, my contacts, my business, my customer, my paid API, my private infra, my domain, my private repo, my partner, or my financial/health/security data** → private skill (`_ALLCAPS`).

**When in doubt, build it private first (`_ALLCAPS`). Promoting `_FOO` → `Foo` later is easy. Discovering a public skill leaks your life is permanent.**

---

## Public Release Readiness (MANDATORY)

**Public skills (`TitleCase`) ship to the world. Private skills (`_ALLCAPS`) never leave the local repo.** Sensitivity is decided by skill name, not by per-file scrubbing at share-time.

### The Bright Line

**Public skill (`TitleCase`) — content rule:**

ONLY templated, safe, public, ready content. Period.

- ✅ Generic instructions any LifeOS user could follow
- ✅ Templated patterns with placeholders for user-specific values
- ✅ Public API references and dependencies on public tools
- ❌ Real names (people, products, companies, customers)
- ❌ Real domains, hostnames, IPs, internal URLs
- ❌ API keys, tokens, credentials, session cookies, OAuth secrets — even example-looking ones
- ❌ Private repo paths or references (`github.com/<org>/<private-repo>`)
- ❌ Customer data, customer-specific workflows, customer engagement context
- ❌ First-person war stories tied to a specific incident, project, or person
- ❌ User-specific filesystem paths (`/Users/<name>/...`, `/home/<name>/...`)
- ❌ Identity-bound preferences (DA name, principal name, partner name, pet name, financial figures, health data)

**Private skill (`_ALLCAPS`) — content rule:**

Anything goes. Real names, real domains, real customers, real credentials-by-reference (env var names, never values), real war stories, real internal infra. The underscore IS the safety boundary. These skills are excluded from release tooling.

### The Decision Test

When you find yourself wanting to write any of the following into a skill body, that skill MUST be `_ALLCAPS`:

| If the skill mentions… | Skill must be |
|------------------------|---------------|
| A specific person's name (yours, your partner's, your team's, a customer's) | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific product name you own or sell | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific customer or client | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific paid API account, billing realm, or subscription | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private domain, hostname, internal IP, or VPN | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private repo, dotfile location, or local infra | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific business process tied to your company | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific financial, health, security, or legal context | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific incident or one-off war story | `_ALLCAPS` |
| Anything that would be wrong, embarrassing, or unsafe in someone else's `~/.claude/` | `_ALLCAPS` |

If none of the above apply and the skill is fully generic — it can be `TitleCase` (public).

### Where Personal Layering Goes for Public Skills

A public skill can be made user-specific at runtime via `~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/PREFERENCES.md`. The skill body stays generic; the user's customization file overlays per-instance context. Use this when a skill is fundamentally generic but benefits from per-user tweaks (preferred voice, default formats, personal taste).

**Do not use SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS to smuggle private content into a public skill.** If the skill *requires* private context to function (real customer name, real API account, real internal infra), it is a private skill — name it `_ALLCAPS` and stop.

### Allowed in Public Skills

- Generic `~/` paths (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/Projects/<tool>/`) — resolve per-user
- Public repo URLs for tools the skill depends on
- Public API endpoints that are conventions, not secrets (e.g., `localhost:31337/notify`)
- Example values clearly marked as placeholders (`<url>`, `<SESSION_ID>`, `test@example.com`)
- Generic env var *names* (never values): `STRIPE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`

### Pre-Flight Grep (Public Skills Only)

Before shipping or modifying any `TitleCase` skill, run:
```bash
rg -i "<your-name>|<your-org>|<your-product>|<your-domain>|/Users/[a-z]+/" ~/.claude/skills/<SkillName>/
```

Zero matches = ready for public release. Any match = either scrub it, move it to SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS, or rename the skill to `_ALLCAPS` and stop pretending it's public. **`_ALLCAPS` skills are exempt from this grep — they are private by design.**

---

## Flat Folder Structure (MANDATORY)

**CRITICAL: Keep folder structure FLAT - maximum 2 levels deep.**

### The Rule

**Maximum depth:** `skills/SkillName/Category/`

### ✅ ALLOWED (2 levels max)

```
skills/SkillName/SKILL.md                    # Skill root
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Create.md         # Workflow - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Tools/Manage.ts             # Tool - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/QuickStartGuide.md          # Context file - in root - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Examples.md                 # Context file - in root - GOOD
```

### ❌ FORBIDDEN (Too deep OR wrong location)

```
skills/SkillName/Resources/Guide.md              # Context files go in root, NOT Resources/
skills/SkillName/Docs/Examples.md                # Context files go in root, NOT Docs/
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Category/File.md      # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Templates/Primitives/File.md    # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Tools/Utils/Helper.ts           # THREE levels - NO
```

### Allowed Subdirectories

**These subdirectories are allowed:**
- **Workflows/** - Execution workflows ONLY
- **Tools/** - Executable scripts/tools ONLY
- **References/** - Extended reference material for large skills (API docs, detailed guides)

**Context files (documentation, guides, references) go in the skill ROOT or in References/.**

**When to use References/:** When SKILL.md exceeds ~500 lines and has substantial reference content (API signatures, detailed examples, troubleshooting guides). Keep SKILL.md as a routing guide; move encyclopedic content to References/.

### Why

1. **Discoverability** - Easy to find files
2. **Simplicity** - Less navigation overhead
3. **Speed** - Faster file operations
4. **Consistency** - Every skill follows same pattern

**If you need to organize many workflows, use clear filenames instead of subdirectories:**

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Flat Folder Structure section)

---

## Dynamic Loading Pattern (Large Skills)

**For skills with SKILL.md > 100 lines:** Use dynamic loading to reduce context on skill invocation.

### How Loading Works

**Session startup:** Only frontmatter loads for routing
**Skill invocation:** Full SKILL.md loads
**Context files:** Load only when workflows reference them

### The Pattern

**SKILL.md** = Minimal (30-50 lines) - loads on skill invocation
- YAML frontmatter with triggers
- Brief description
- Workflow routing table
- Quick reference
- Pointers to context files

**Additional .md files** = Context files - SOPs for specific aspects (loaded on-demand)
- These are Standard Operating Procedures, not just documentation
- They provide specific handling instructions
- Can reference Workflows/, Tools/, etc.

### 🚨 CRITICAL: NO Context/ Subdirectory 🚨

**NEVER create Context/ or Docs/ subdirectories.**

Additional .md files ARE the context files. They live **directly in skill root**.

**WRONG:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
└── Context/              ❌ NEVER CREATE THIS
    └── Aesthetic.md
```

**CORRECT:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
├── Aesthetic.md          ✅ Context file in skill root
├── Examples.md           ✅ Context file in skill root
└── Tools.md              ✅ Context file in skill root
```

**The skill directory IS the context.**

### Example Structure

```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md              # 40 lines - minimal routing
├── Aesthetic.md          # Context file - SOP for aesthetic
├── Examples.md           # Context file - SOP for examples
├── Tools.md              # Context file - SOP for tools
├── Workflows/            # Workflows
│   └── Essay.md
└── Tools/                # CLI tools
    └── Generate.ts
```

### Minimal SKILL.md Template

```markdown
---
name: SkillName
description: Create, test, and optimize LifeOS skills — scaffolding, effectiveness testing, description optimization. USE WHEN create skill, new skill, validate skill, test skill, improve skill, optimize description.
---

# SkillName

Brief description.

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger | Workflow |
|---------|----------|
| "trigger" | `Workflows/WorkflowName.md` |

## Quick Reference

**Key points** (3-5 bullet points)

**Full Documentation:**
- Detail 1: `SkillSearch('skillname detail1')` → loads Detail1.md
- Detail 2: `SkillSearch('skillname detail2')` → loads Detail2.md
```

### When To Use

✅ **Use dynamic loading for:**
- SKILL.md > 100 lines
- Multiple documentation sections
- Extensive API reference
- Detailed examples

❌ **Don't use for:**
- Simple skills (< 50 lines)
- Pure utility wrappers (use LIFEOS/TOOLS.md instead)

### Benefits

- **Token Savings:** 70%+ reduction on skill invocation (when full docs not needed)
- **Organization:** SKILL.md = routing, context files = SOPs for specific aspects
- **Efficiency:** Workflows load only what they actually need
- **Maintainability:** Easier to update individual sections

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Dynamic Loading Pattern section)

---


## Workflow Routing

### Structure Workflows (scaffolding and conventions)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **CreateSkill** | "create a new skill" | `Workflows/CreateSkill.md` |
| **ValidateSkill** | "validate skill", "check skill" | `Workflows/ValidateSkill.md` |
| **UpdateSkill** | "update skill", "add workflow" | `Workflows/UpdateSkill.md` |
| **CanonicalizeSkill** | "canonicalize", "fix skill structure" | `Workflows/CanonicalizeSkill.md` |

### Effectiveness Workflows (testing and optimization)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **TestSkill** | "test skill", "does this skill work", "skill not working" | `Workflows/TestSkill.md` |
| **ImproveSkill** | "improve skill", "skill quality", "fix skill instructions" | `Workflows/ImproveSkill.md` |
| **OptimizeDescription** | "optimize description", "skill not triggering", "trigger accuracy" | `Workflows/OptimizeDescription.md` |

## Skill Types (Choose Before Building)

Before creating any skill, identify which of the 9 types it is (from Anthropic's internal skill taxonomy, Thariq Shihipar, Mar 2026). The type shapes structure and testing decisions.

| Type | Focus | Key Structure | Example |
|------|-------|---------------|---------|
| 1. Library/API Reference | Gotchas, edge cases Claude gets wrong | Lightweight, gotchas-heavy, reference snippets | HonoReference, D1Reference |
| 2. Product Validation | Test/verify code works | State assertions, browser automation, output recording | Browser |
| 3. Data Fetching | Connect to data systems | Credential refs, query patterns, dashboard pointers | USMetrics, _METRICS |
| 4. Business Process | Automate repetitive workflows | Execution logs, consistency tracking | _CLICKUP, _BROADCAST |
| 5. Code Scaffolding | Generate framework boilerplate | Template files, project-aware scripts | CreateCLI, CreateSkill |
| 6. Code Quality | Enforce standards, review | Deterministic scripts, hook integration | /simplify, /code-review |
| 7. CI/CD & Deployment | Deploy with safety patterns | Pre-deploy checks, smoke tests, rollback | (gap — needs Deploy skill) |
| 8. Operations Runbooks | Map phenomena to diagnostics | Phenomenon → tool → query → report | _HEALTHCHECK |
| 9. Infrastructure Ops | Maintenance with safety guardrails | Safety gates, audit logging, orphan detection | _LIFEOS, _DOTFILES |

## Skill Writing Guidance

When writing or improving skill instructions, follow these principles from Anthropic's skill-creator methodology and Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026):

### Core Principles

- **Don't state the obvious.** Claude is competent at programming and knows codebases. Focus on information that **breaks Claude's default patterns** — things it gets wrong without guidance. Test: "Would Claude do this wrong without being told?" If not, remove it.
- **Explain the why, not just the what.** Models with good theory of mind + clear reasoning outperform models with rigid constraints. Instead of "ALWAYS use 3 bullets", explain why bullets matter for the audience.
- **Keep it lean.** The context window is a public good. Remove instructions that don't improve output. If test transcripts show the agent wasting time on unproductive steps, cut them. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines.
- **Cut intensifier-only lines.** Stating a rule once is the instruction. `MANDATORY`, `CRITICAL`, "not optional", and a third restatement add volume, not constraint — the model obeys specificity and code, not emphasis. Delete any line whose only content is shouting a rule stated elsewhere. Watch `## Best Practices` / `## Tips` sections: they collect default-restating filler ("be thorough", "keep it simple", "validate carefully"). Run the delete-test in `Prompting/Standards.md` § Signal-to-Noise on every line: cut it, and restore only if you can name the specific non-default behavior it forces.
- **Generalize, don't overfit.** Fix underlying patterns, not specific test failures. The skill will be used on many prompts beyond your test set.
- **Bundle repeated work.** If test agents all independently wrote similar helper scripts, add that script to Tools/ so every future invocation benefits.
- **Set appropriate degrees of freedom.** Match specificity to task fragility. Database migrations need exact commands; code reviews need general direction.
- **Don't over-constrain.** Skills are reused heavily. Avoid overly specific instructions. Provide needed information but leave flexibility for different contexts.

### Description Best Practices

- **Descriptions are for models, not humans.** The description is injected into the system prompt. Claude reads it to decide whether to invoke the skill.
- **Descriptions should be slightly pushy.** Models tend to undertrigger. Name specific scenarios even if the user might not explicitly mention the skill.
- **Include negative triggers for confusable skills.** Add "NOT FOR" clauses when skills share vocabulary: `"NOT FOR web pentesting (use WebAssessment)"`.
- **Undertriggering signals:** Skill doesn't load when it should, users manually invoking it.
- **Overtriggering signals:** Skill loads for irrelevant queries, users disabling it.

### Gotchas Section (MANDATORY)

Every skill MUST have a `## Gotchas` section after the workflow routing table. Thariq: "The highest information density in any Skill comes from gotchas sections."

Populate with:
- API quirks Claude doesn't know about
- Common mistakes observed during usage
- Ordering/sequencing requirements that aren't obvious
- Edge cases that cause silent failures

**Gotchas accumulate over time.** After every skill failure, add the lesson.

### BPE (Bitter-Pilled Engineering) Check

Before finalizing any skill, ask: **"Would a smarter model make this skill unnecessary?"**

- **Anti-fragile (keep):** Verification harnesses, data pipelines, tool wrappers, accumulated gotchas, deterministic scripts
- **Fragile (question):** CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, elaborate reasoning scaffolding

Focus skills on knowledge Claude can't derive (failure modes, API quirks), tools Claude can't replicate (API calls, automation), and workflows that benefit from consistency.

### Progressive Disclosure (from Anthropic)

Three levels of information loading — use this to manage large skills:
1. **Level 1 (YAML frontmatter):** Always in system prompt. Triggering info only.
2. **Level 2 (SKILL.md body):** Loaded when skill is invoked. Routing + key guidance.
3. **Level 3 (Reference files):** Root-level `.md` files or `References/` subdirectory loaded on demand.

Tell Claude what files exist; it will read them when appropriate. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines — if over, extract detailed content to reference files.

### Testing Best Practices (from Anthropic)

Three testing levels for skills:
1. **Manual testing** — Run queries and observe behavior
2. **Scripted testing** — Automate test cases (use TestSkill workflow)
3. **Programmatic testing** — Build evaluation suites (use Evals skill)

**Evaluation-driven development:** Define what "this skill working" looks like before building the skill. Iterate on a single challenging task until Claude succeeds, then extract the winning approach.

### On-Demand Hook Pattern (from Anthropic)

Skills can include hooks that activate only when invoked, remaining effective for the session:
- `/careful` — Intercept dangerous commands (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, force-push)
- `/freeze` — Block edits outside specific directories
- `/audit` — Log all tool calls for session review

*All guidance above derived from Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026), Anthropic's official skill guide, and platform documentation.*

## Examples

**Example 1: Create a new skill from scratch**
```
User: "Create a skill for managing my recipes"
→ Invokes CreateSkill workflow
→ Reads SkillSystem.md for structure requirements
→ Creates skill directory with TitleCase naming
→ Creates SKILL.md, Workflows/, Tools/
→ Suggests running TestSkill to verify effectiveness
```

**Example 2: Fix an existing skill that's not routing properly**
```
User: "The research skill isn't triggering - validate it"
→ Invokes ValidateSkill workflow
→ Checks SKILL.md against canonical format
→ Verifies TitleCase naming and USE WHEN triggers
→ Reports compliance issues with fixes
```

**Example 3: Test if a skill actually helps**
```
User: "Test the Blogging skill to see if it's effective"
→ Invokes TestSkill workflow
→ Generates 3 realistic test prompts
→ Spawns with-skill and baseline agents in parallel
→ Compares outputs, presents results
→ Iterates with ImproveSkill based on feedback
```

**Example 4: Skill isn't triggering on relevant prompts**
```
User: "The Security skill doesn't trigger when I ask about pentesting"
→ Invokes OptimizeDescription workflow
→ Generates 20 should/shouldn't-trigger queries
→ Tests description accuracy via subagents
→ Rewrites description, re-tests, reports improvement
```

**Example 5: Improve a skill that produces weak output**
```
User: "The research skill output is too verbose — improve it"
→ Invokes ImproveSkill workflow
→ Reads skill + user feedback
→ Diagnoses root cause (over-specified instructions)
→ Rewrites with reasoning instead of rigid MUSTs
→ Suggests TestSkill to verify improvement
```

## Gotchas

- **Descriptions cap at 1024 chars, and this file's own description sat at ~1022 — 2 to spare** (2026-06-13 audit). It was cut to ~770 on 2026-08-15 by moving enforcement prose to the `## Enforcement` section; every USE WHEN trigger was kept, because descriptions are what make a skill fire. Re-measure before saving any frontmatter edit, and never buy headroom by deleting triggers.
- **Two `## Workflow Routing` headers exist in this file** — the first (~l.284) is inside the embedded template example, the second (~l.323) is the real one. Header-scanning tools must take the LAST match, not the first. Match on line-anchored `^## Workflow Routing`; a plain substring search also hits an inline mention in the UpdateSkill instructions and returns three.
- **Reading this skill's workflows and executing the steps by hand is the handrolling anti-pattern** — `skills/CLAUDE.md` requires invoking the skill, not imitating it. The skill that mandates Gotchas sections went without one until 2026-06-13; treat checklist items as applying to this skill too.

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"CreateSkill","workflow":"WORKFLOW_USED","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

Replace `WORKFLOW_USED` with the workflow executed, `8_WORD_SUMMARY` with a brief input description, and `SECONDS` with approximate wall-clock time. Log `status: "error"` if the workflow failed.

# Claude Stack Doctor

One command surfaces every known silent-failure class in the automation/memory stack. Run it before debugging anything by hand.

## Quick start

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1
```

Exit 0 = all clear. Exit 1 = the VERDICT line lists issue codes. Report the findings to the user, then apply the matching fix below.

**This machine is macOS** (migrated 2026-08-05). Jobs are **launchd user agents** in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, not Task Scheduler. The script is PowerShell only because `pwsh` runs it natively; it checks launchd. PowerShell on macOS normalises `\` inside a path string to `/`, so the script's mixed separators resolve correctly — verified 2026-08-29. Do not "fix" them.

Useful launchd commands:
```bash
launchctl list | grep keystone                                    # loaded jobs + last exit code
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>                  # live schedule and state
launchctl bootout  gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>               # unload
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.<name>.plist   # reload
```
Edit a schedule with `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour <n>" <plist>`, then bootout + bootstrap. **A plist edit alone does nothing until it is reloaded.**

## Weekly scheduled run

launchd agent `com.keystone.stackdoctor` (Mondays 10:30) runs `scripts/weekly-check.ps1`: the same read-only check, unattended. On failure it appends a one-line summary to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at every session start per CLAUDE.md) and the full output is always in `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`. When a session surfaces such an entry, run this skill interactively to diagnose and fix, then clear the entry from `.errors.log`.

**Clearing `.errors.log`:** shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`. Use `cp /dev/null <file>`. There is no `truncate` binary on this machine. Archive first — the lines are often live issues, not stale history:
```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

## Known failure classes and fixes

These four classes have each bitten more than once (evidence: daily logs 2026-04 → 2026-07). Match the issue code to its fix:

### `task:*` / `task-stale:*` — launchd agent failed or didn't run
1. Read the `action:` line the script printed and run that exact command **manually in a foreground terminal** — launchd discards stdout unless the plist sets `StandardOutPath`; foreground shows the real error.
2. Known root causes: executable referenced without a full path (launchd agents get a minimal PATH — always use full paths like `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`, and set `EnvironmentVariables:PATH` in the plist); a plist edited but never `bootout`+`bootstrap`ed, so the old schedule is still live; the job firing at an hour the required volume is unmounted (see `backup-*`).
3. `launchctl list | grep keystone` shows each job's **last exit code** in column 2. A non-zero there with no output means the script's own log is the only evidence — check `~/.claude/scripts/logs/` and for a `*.log` beside the script.

### `venv-missing` / `venv-broken` — Python venv rot
The script checks `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/.venv/bin/python`.
macOS root causes: a Homebrew `python3` major-version bump orphans venvs built against the old interpreter; a `uv` reinstall or relocation breaks tools that hardcode `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` (CLAUDE.md forbids relocating it for this reason).

---
name: backup
description: Run the KeystoneOS daily backup on demand (git-push the memory repos, rsync state to Google Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD, reindex memsearch), then report what was saved and what was skipped. Use when the user says "/backup", "run the backup", "back up now", "back my stuff up", "did the backup run", "the backup failed", "I left the laptop off — catch up the backup", or when a session-start HOOK FAILURE names daily-backup. The scheduled launchd job only fires if the Mac is awake at 09:00, so this is the manual catch-up path. NOT FOR whole-stack health checks (use claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` right now. Same script the `com.keystone.dailybackup`
launchd agent runs at 09:00 daily — this is the on-demand path for when the Mac was shut at 09:00.

## Run it

Do not pre-check anything. Run first, report after.

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
```

Use a Bash `timeout` of at least `600000` (10 min). The memsearch INDEX step is ~75s of a ~85s
healthy run; the default 2-min timeout can survive it, but a grown corpus will not.

## Read the verdict from state, not from the tail

```bash
cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json
```

`status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. That file is the authority.
The tail is for diagnosing, not for deciding.

## Then clear the stale hook error, if any

A failed run appends a line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`, which is surfaced
as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. A later successful run does **not** clear it. If `status`
is now `OK` and the file contains only `daily-backup:` lines, archive and empty it:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

If any non-`daily-backup` line is present, leave the file alone and tell the user what else is in it.
Shell truncation (`: > file`) under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule
`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`, and there is no `truncate` binary here — use `cp /dev/null`.

## Report

Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.

## Gotchas

Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.

## Gotchas

**Safe to ignore — expected on a healthy run:**
- `SNAP skip (missing): ~/.codex/memories` — that path has never existed.
- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED` — deliberate.

**Real gaps — always surface these to the user:**
- `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture SKIPPED`
  — the run still reports `OK` with 0 errors, but **untracked, gitignored, and uncommitted-modified
  files were not saved anywhere.** GitHub and Google Drive cover only committed and pushed work.
  Tell the user to plug in CRASHBOX and run again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.
- `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?` — the Drive app is not running.
  Start it, then re-run.
- `PUSH ERR ... Could not resolve host: github.com` — a network blip, not a repo problem. Confirm
  with `ping -c1 github.com`, then just re-run; the commits are already made locally and will push.
  (Seen 2026-09-04 09:05: both `global-memory` and `skills` failed this way and a re-run fixed both.)
- `repo-diverged:<name>` — automation will never merge. Reconcile that repo by hand.

**Other:**
- Every log line appears **twice** for launchd runs and once for manual runs. The script both writes
  to the log file and prints to stdout, and the plist captures stdout to the same file. Not a bug —
  do not "fix" it, and do not read doubled lines as two attempts.
- The script is PowerShell only because `pwsh` runs it natively. It manages launchd, not Task
  Scheduler; the Windows original is parked at `daily-backup.ps1.win-orig`.
- `-DryRun` is the only parameter. Use it to preview without writing.

## Examples

**Example 1: routine catch-up**
```
User: "run the backup"
→ Runs the script, reads backup-state.json (status OK, 0 errors)
→ "Backup done, no errors. Everything pushed and copied to Drive.
   CRASHBOX SSD wasn't plugged in, so uncommitted files were not saved.
   Plug it in and run /backup again if you have unsaved work."
```

**Example 2: session start shows a hook failure**
```
User: "the backup failed this morning — fix it"
→ Greps daily-backup.log for the error codes → DNS failure on both pushes
→ Confirms github.com reachable, re-runs the script → status OK
→ Archives and empties .errors.log so the warning stops appearing
```

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence (commit+push to KeystoneOS is standing-authorized per `feedback-auto-commit-push`; for any OTHER repo with changes, commit locally and list the push as an open item instead of pushing).

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` in every repo touched this session (check cwd first, then any repo mentioned in the conversation; if session context is thin, check `KeystoneOS` and any `DEV/` repo with commits dated today).
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- KeystoneOS: stage, commit with a descriptive message, push. Authorized.
- Other repos with changes: commit locally with a descriptive message; do NOT push without asking — list it in the final report instead.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Never push to a repo other than KeystoneOS without explicit approval.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# 2026-09-04 — On-demand `/backup` skill + full SSD backup run

## What was being worked on and why

Eric asked to run the daily backup and to turn it into a skill he can invoke at
will. His stated premise ("we don't have it scheduled") was wrong — the launchd
agent `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 daily — but his reasoning was
right: the Mac is often off at 09:00, so a scheduled-only job silently skips days.
An on-demand path genuinely did not exist.

## Decisions made (and why)

- **Skill named `backup`, lowercase-kebab.** Matches its closest sibling
  `claude-stack-doctor`. The `TitleCase`/`_ALLCAPS` convention in
  `~/.claude/skills/CLAUDE.md` describes public-vs-private packaging; every ops
  skill actually loaded in this workspace is lowercase-kebab, and `name:`
  frontmatter must equal the directory name.
- **The skill reads `backup-state.json`, not the exit code or the log tail.**
  The script can exit 0 while a target was skipped. `status` + `errors[]` in that
  file is the only authority.
- **The skill must always name a skipped target.** A run with the SSD unplugged
  reports `OK` with 0 errors while untracked/gitignored/uncommitted files were
  saved nowhere. Reporting "backup complete" there is the exact failure mode the
  skill exists to prevent.
- **Job count is the completeness signal, not the error count.** 9 jobs OK
  without the SSD vs 31 jobs OK with it.
- **`.errors.log` must be cleared by hand after a fixed failure.** The script only
  appends; a later success never clears it, so the HOOK FAILURE block keeps
  appearing at every session start. Clear with `cp /dev/null` — dcg rule
  `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home` blocks `: > file` under `$HOME`,
  and there is no `truncate` binary on this machine.

## What actually happened

1. The 09:05 scheduled run failed with `repo-push:global-memory` and
   `repo-push:skills`. Root cause from the log: `Could not resolve host:
   github.com` — a transient DNS blip, not a repo or auth problem. Commits were
   already made locally; a re-run pushed them cleanly.
2. First manual re-run: `OK`, 0 errors, but **9 jobs** — CRASHBOX SSD was not
   mounted, so the orphan and working-tree capture was skipped entirely.
3. Eric said the SSD was connected, but `diskutil list external` printed nothing
   and no USB/Thunderbolt device appeared at all. Diagnosed as a cable or port
   problem, not software. A charge-only USB-C cable is the usual culprit; the fast
   check is `diskutil list external` printing nothing.
4. After the cable/port fix: `/dev/disk4`, `CRASHBOX`, 500 GB, 437 Gi free,
   mounted at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX`. Full run: **0 errors, 31 jobs OK, 7,801 files
   written.** Receipt `run-20260904-134638.txt`. Per-folder freshness confirmed
   the point of the exercise: `DEV-working-tree` 7 fresh, `DEV-nonrepo` 106 fresh,
   `DEV-repo-data` 2,458 fresh.

- `~/.claude/skills/backup/SKILL.md` — new. Committed and pushed to the
  `claude-skills` repo.
- `~/DEV/COMMANDS.md` — added a `/backup` row to the slash-command table and

- `~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl` — appended a CreateSkill row.
- `~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json` — now `status: OK`, `errors: []`,

Plug in CRASHBOX, then type `/backup` in Claude Code. That is the whole thing.

- The header comment in `daily-backup.ps1` still claims "Runs daily at 00:30".

- Log lines appear **twice** for launchd runs (the script writes to the log file

=== Tier A backup memory ===
---
name: backup-sync-system
description: "Nightly backup/sync architecture and its traps — two-writer root cause, manifest classification rules, Milvus is NOT in the memsearch path, dry-run can't verify writes"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3db720f8-cca5-4aed-96cd-e7ac4a95ab2d
  modified: 2026-09-03T18:15:45.092Z
---

**Current state (2026-09-03).** Two backup runs happen on most days, and the 09-02 entry was
right about that — but **not** because reconcile hard-codes the backup. The real mechanism,
traced 09-03:

`keystone-reconcile.ps1` is a **generic make-up engine**. It has no mention of `daily-backup` at
all; it loops the registry at `DEV/KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` and calls
`run-job.ps1 -Job <id> -Trigger reconcile -MadeUp` for any job with no success recorded today.
The `daily-backup` job is in that registry with `reconcile: true`, `graceMinutes: 60`,
`maxAttemptsPerDay: 2`, and `makeupWindow: 07:00-20:00`. Its `successProbe` greps today's
`daily-backup.log` for `daily-backup end: OK`. So:

- **If no successful run is recorded by 07:00, reconcile replays it** → the ~07:00-07:10 run.
- **launchd `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 regardless** → the second run.
- **Run the backup by hand before 07:00 and reconcile skips it** ("already succeeded today").
  Confirmed 09-03: a 06:15 manual run logged `OK` at 06:25, and no 07:00 run happened.

Registry inconsistency worth knowing: `jobs.json` records `schedule.at: "00:30"` while the live
plist fires at 09:00. The make-up window is what actually drives the 07:00 replay, so the stale
`at` has not bitten yet. Still true: `launchctl ... runs = 0` proves nothing — read the log.
Receipts cluster only on days CRASHBOX is attached: a mount gap, not a schedule gap.

**"Scheduled runs cannot push" is NOT yet established — and the two contexts differ.** On
2026-09-03 the **09:00 launchd** run pushed `global-memory` cleanly and ended `OK (0 errors)`:
no `PUSH FAILED`, no `PUSH ERR`. But the **reconcile/`run-job.ps1`** context — which is where the
09-02 07:08 and 08-13 07:00 failures happened — **was not exercised that day**, because the manual
06:15 run pre-empted the replay. Do not read 09-03 as clearing the gap; it only clears launchd.
`daily-backup.ps1:74` no longer swallows the reason: the `Out-Null` was replaced 09-03 with
captured output that logs `REPO <name> : PUSH ERR | <text>` on failure only. **The error text will
only appear on a day nobody runs the backup by hand before 07:00.** Diagnose from that line rather
than assuming a credential gap. `daily-backup.err` is stale (last written 2026-08-06); never read
it as current. Manual remedy after a failed push is still `git -C <repo> push origin main` for
SecondBrain, `.claude/global-memory`, `.claude`.

**SSD layout:** non-repo DEV dirs land in `DEV-nonrepo/`, **not** `DEV/` — there is no `DEV/`
on CRASHBOX (roots are `DEV-nonrepo/`, `DEV-repo-data/`, `DEV-working-tree/`, `claude/`,
`codex/`, `gemini/`, `SecondBrain/`, `_receipts/`). `._`-prefixed files beside every real file
are normal AppleDouble xattr sidecars on exFAT, not corruption or duplication.

The nightly backup is `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (pwsh, launchd
`com.keystone.dailybackup`), driven by `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`, logging to
`~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`. `~/.claude` is itself the `dotclaude` repo.
Workflow docs live in `~/DEV/Bucket` (`docs/SYSTEM-HEALTH-FINDINGS.md`,
`docs/AGENT-FIX-PROMPT.md`, `docs/FIX-STATUS-2026-08-14.md`).

## The root cause behind most "divergence" symptoms — CLOSED 2026-08-14

The retired **Windows box was still running `daily-backup.ps1` and pushing to the shared
repos** (SecondBrain, dotclaude, claude-skills, claude-global-memory). Two writers on one
set of repos manufactured `repo-diverged:SecondBrain` nightly. Identified by the
commit-message format `chore: daily backup sync YYYY-MM-DD [auto]`, generated at
`daily-backup.ps1:62`.

**Retired 2026-08-14**: all 9 KeystoneOS/MorningBriefing scheduled tasks disabled (not
unregistered) on the Windows box; all four repos left at 0 ahead / 0 behind. It contributed
no unique history since 08-05 — only two append-only Windows failure logs, preserved
byte-identical to `~/Desktop/windows-retirement-2026-08-14/` on that machine and
deliberately **not** pushed (origin had already untracked `.memsearch-index.log` in
`a0e58c9`; committing would have undone a Mac-side decision).

Residual, by design — the box is meant to stay usable:
- **Session hooks still write.** `settings.json` `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks write
  `global-memory/transcripts/`, so interactive Claude Code use there re-dirties that repo.
  It cannot *diverge* it — nothing pushes on a schedule anymore. (That Stop hook is
  currently broken there anyway: `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on a mangled
  `C:\Program Files\Git\...\transcript-capture.js` path.)
- **`daily-backup.ps1` on Windows is still the macOS port** and still buggy. It is inert
  because the task is disabled, not because it was repaired.
- Three non-KeystoneOS tasks left enabled (`CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder`,
  `DailyGmailDigest`, `Refresh_All_Data`) — all operate under the Windows `~/Desktop/DEV`
  and touch none of the four repos.

## Manifest classification — get this right, it routes athlete data

`backup-manifest.json` is default-deny: any `~/DEV` dir absent from `paths[]` fails the
health check. Adding an entry requires a human class call:

| class | destinations |

### Orphans are a symptom, not the cause

Two `rsync --server` receivers were **orphaned to PPID 1** (started 13:55 and 14:33). It is
tempting to call them the blocker; the timeline refutes it — the **10:31:54 run hung at the
identical point** (last line `SNAP skip (missing): .codex/memories`, no end line) while the
oldest surviving orphan did not exist until 13:55. `kill` on both orphans did not unblock
the live pair either.

Why they accumulate: **`daily-backup.ps1` contains no `pkill` at all** (verified by grep —
do not go looking for one). The anchored `pkill -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` belongs to an *ad-hoc
wrapper used interactively in another session*. That pattern matches only the client, whose
`argv[0]` is the full path; the `--server` child's `argv[0]` is bare `rsync`, so
`pgrep -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` returns the client alone. Every kill-and-retry therefore strands
one more receiver. If that wrapper is reused, match on `-x rsync` or the destination path.

### ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 17:00 — it is not rsync

Ran the copy in the foreground with `-avv`, unpiped. It printed ~99 lines of
`... is uptodate` and froze mid-filename. Then:

- `sample <receiver-pid>` showed the process blocked in **`__mmap`** — one frame, not moving.
- `lsof` on it showed FD 5 open on a specific **destination** file:
  `codex/sessions/2026/05/08/rollout-2026-05-08T17-14-58-019e09a8-*.jsonl`.
- **`head -c 512` on that destination file hangs by itself**, with zero rsync processes
  running. A plain read. So the file is unreadable through DriveFS.
- A 44-file sample elsewhere in the same mirror read instantly, so it is **specific files,
  not the mount**.

The files are **DriveFS placeholders** — uploaded to Google, then evicted from the local
cache. Census of the destination on 2026-08-14: 256 files, **122 materialized (48.5 MB on
disk), 134 placeholder-only (240.7 MB logical, 0 bytes local)**. Source is 256/256
materialized. Detect with `stat -f '%b %z'`: blocks==0 with a nonzero logical size means
the content is not local. Reading one forces an on-demand fetch, and that fetch stalls —
which is what blocks `__mmap`. rsync was the victim, not the cause. **Do not chase rsync
flags**; the block happens at open, before any comparison strategy applies.

**This inverts the problem: the backup is fine, the verification is what's broken.** All
256 files are on Google's servers. Nothing is missing. What fails is the *next* run's
attempt to re-read them to confirm they match. Never conclude "the snapshot is broken"
from this failure mode.

Also: `du -sh` on the destination reports the *local cache* (48 MB), not the logical 289 MB.
Both numbers are true and mean different things — do not treat the gap as missing data.

Diagnostic sequence that worked, reuse it: `sample <pid>` for the blocking syscall →
`lsof -p <pid>` for the file it is on → bounded `head -c` on that path to prove the
filesystem, not the tool, is at fault.

Finder context menu (there is no CLI or xattr for it — the app ships no control surface).

- The **download** queue fails, not just uploads: `merger.cc:969:ProcessDownloadEvent` +

file into a placeholder needing re-download, feeding the exact mechanism that is failing —
122 readable files could become 0. If DriveFS is repaired, do it by signing out and back in

**Final mechanism**: files Drive has evicted from local cache are placeholders. Fetching a
placeholder through DriveFS is *unreliable* — usually fast, sometimes stalling for tens of
minutes. rsync blocking on such a fetch is the entire "wedge". Proof it is a slow fetch and
not a poisoned file: the file that hung four separate times **now reads instantly**, and its
blocks went 0 → 770,048 — the repeated read attempts eventually completed the fetch. Six

nothing corrupt. The scan itself moved the mirror from 122 → 230 materialized (48.5 → 161.8 MB

macOS marks I/O wait `U`, not `D`; a `D`-state grep finds nothing and proves nothing.

Probably (unverified): the Claude Code shell and the launchd/reconcile jobs are different TCC
principals, so this prompt should not recur for the scheduled runs — but it may fire once per new

runs unblock *together* the moment access is granted and race onto the SSD — the two-writer
corruption this whole system exists to prevent.

suppresses the replay; one finishing after 07:00 can collide with it.

## `snapshot:sessions` — evidence from a live reproduction, 2026-08-14 15:20 (stack-doctor)

Caught the hang in progress and narrowed it. **Root cause still open** — this section is
evidence, not a verdict. Everything below is measured, not inferred:

- **It is a hang, not a slow transfer.** Four rsync processes (client `-a ... codex/sessions/`,
  its `--server` receiver, plus two older receivers) sat at **0.01–0.03 s of CPU across
  34–85 minutes** of wall clock. Zero progress, not slow progress.
- **Nothing is left to copy.** The mirror is **256/256 files** — the previously-missing
  `2026/08/06/rollout-*.jsonl` is present. A complete mirror still hangs.
- **The mount is healthy.** A recursive `find` over the destination returned 256 files
  promptly, and `touch` inside the exact hung directory succeeded instantly. Reads *and*
  writes both work, so this is not a wedged DriveFS/FUSE mount.
- **The wedged processes ignore SIGTERM** (still alive minutes later in `S` state) — they
  are blocked inside a call that neither returns nor delivers signals.
- **Dry runs cannot see it**: `-n` completes clean, live runs hang. Another instance of the
  "`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path" trap above.

### Orphans are a symptom, not the cause

Two `rsync --server` receivers were **orphaned to PPID 1** (started 13:55 and 14:33). It is
tempting to call them the blocker; the timeline refutes it — the **10:31:54 run hung at the
identical point** (last line `SNAP skip (missing): .codex/memories`, no end line) while the
oldest surviving orphan did not exist until 13:55. `kill` on both orphans did not unblock
the live pair either.

Why they accumulate: **`daily-backup.ps1` contains no `pkill` at all** (verified by grep —
do not go looking for one). The anchored `pkill -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` belongs to an *ad-hoc
wrapper used interactively in another session*. That pattern matches only the client, whose
`argv[0]` is the full path; the `--server` child's `argv[0]` is bare `rsync`, so
`pgrep -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` returns the client alone. Every kill-and-retry therefore strands
one more receiver. If that wrapper is reused, match on `-x rsync` or the destination path.

### ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 17:00 — it is not rsync

Ran the copy in the foreground with `-avv`, unpiped. It printed ~99 lines of
`... is uptodate` and froze mid-filename. Then:

- `sample <receiver-pid>` showed the process blocked in **`__mmap`** — one frame, not moving.
- `lsof` on it showed FD 5 open on a specific **destination** file:
  `codex/sessions/2026/05/08/rollout-2026-05-08T17-14-58-019e09a8-*.jsonl`.
- **`head -c 512` on that destination file hangs by itself**, with zero rsync processes
  running. A plain read. So the file is unreadable through DriveFS.
- A 44-file sample elsewhere in the same mirror read instantly, so it is **specific files,
  not the mount**.

The files are **DriveFS placeholders** — uploaded to Google, then evicted from the local
cache. Census of the destination on 2026-08-14: 256 files, **122 materialized (48.5 MB on
disk), 134 placeholder-only (240.7 MB logical, 0 bytes local)**. Source is 256/256
materialized. Detect with `stat -f '%b %z'`: blocks==0 with a nonzero logical size means
the content is not local. Reading one forces an on-demand fetch, and that fetch stalls —
which is what blocks `__mmap`. rsync was the victim, not the cause. **Do not chase rsync
flags**; the block happens at open, before any comparison strategy applies.

**This inverts the problem: the backup is fine, the verification is what's broken.** All
256 files are on Google's servers. Nothing is missing. What fails is the *next* run's
attempt to re-read them to confirm they match. Never conclude "the snapshot is broken"
from this failure mode.

Also: `du -sh` on the destination reports the *local cache* (48 MB), not the logical 289 MB.
Both numbers are true and mean different things — do not treat the gap as missing data.

Diagnostic sequence that worked, reuse it: `sample <pid>` for the blocking syscall →
`lsof -p <pid>` for the file it is on → bounded `head -c` on that path to prove the
filesystem, not the tool, is at fault.

**Attempted fix that DID NOT WORK**: pinning `My Drive/Backups` "Available offline" via the
Finder context menu (there is no CLI or xattr for it — the app ships no control surface).
Eric pinned it 2026-08-14 17:30. Result: **one** file materialized, then flat for 5 minutes
(133 placeholders, 49.2 MB, unchanged). Restarting Drive did not help either.

**DriveFS on this Mac is itself unhealthy** — this is the real blocker, not rsync and not
the pin:
- It refused a graceful `osascript quit` for 20s and needed SIGKILL. Its log emitted
  `crashpad ... ThreadsStuck` every 6s. Restarting cleared the stuck threads but nothing else.
- The **download** queue fails, not just uploads: `merger.cc:969:ProcessDownloadEvent` +
  `HandleFailedChange [DownloadMergeQueueItem]`. DriveFS cannot pull content *down*.
- Signs of local DB damage: `item_query_handler.cc:1135:OnGetItemIds Ignoring item
  local-376561 that's missing from ...`.
- NOT quota: 671 GB used of 5.5 TB.

**Do not clear the DriveFS content cache as the remedy.** It converts every materialized
file into a placeholder needing re-download, feeding the exact mechanism that is failing —
122 readable files could become 0. If DriveFS is repaired, do it by signing out and back in
to force a DB rebuild, deliberately, with time to watch it.

### RESOLVED 2026-08-14 — the backup was never broken, the verification was

**Final mechanism**: files Drive has evicted from local cache are placeholders. Fetching a
placeholder through DriveFS is *unreliable* — usually fast, sometimes stalling for tens of
minutes. rsync blocking on such a fetch is the entire "wedge". Proof it is a slow fetch and
not a poisoned file: the file that hung four separate times **now reads instantly**, and its
blocks went 0 → 770,048 — the repeated read attempts eventually completed the fetch. Six
other placeholders read fine first try. Nothing was corrupt.

**`~/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh` (`0d2edb5`) is now the way to verify.** It
compares the Drive API's server-side `md5Checksum` against a local md5 — metadata only, no
DriveFS read, batched ~25 names per query. First run on `~/.codex/sessions`:
**256/256 verified, 0 mismatch, 0 missing.** The snapshot that logged `FAILED` for days was
complete and byte-correct the whole time.

Do not "fix" this by deleting Drive copies. Both files that hung were verified byte-identical
to source *before* anything was touched — deleting would have destroyed a good backup to
repair a read path.

**It is plain fetch latency, scaling with file size** — no mystery left. A full read-scan of
all 256 files with a 6s per-file cap: 33 stalled, and those averaged **2,301 KB vs 1,156 KB
for the set overall** (max 15.8 MB). Bigger file, longer fetch. Nothing file-specific,
nothing corrupt. The scan itself moved the mirror from 122 → 230 materialized (48.5 → 161.8 MB
local), which is exactly what "reading materializes it" predicts.

Caution when testing this: **reading a file materializes it**, so any scan warms the cache and
a later run passes for reasons that will not hold once Drive evicts again. Timestamp results
and never treat a post-scan rsync run as a clean verification.

**Google Drive is mirroring `~/DEV` as a device-backup folder named "My Mac"**, including

of the `PRECONDITION_FAILED` storms on `FETCH_HEAD` and the stuck threads in `drive_fs.txt`,
and therefore of the slow placeholder fetches upstream.

Proof (not inference): local `~/DEV/*/.git/FETCH_HEAD` all stamped 18:22:09 while Drive's
server copies read `2026-08-14T23:22:09Z` — same second — and the Drive parent chain resolves
`FETCH_HEAD → .git → DataBase_GPS_Reporting → DEV → My Mac`.

**`OneDrive-Import` was a red herring** — it holds 22 `.git` dirs / 7,292 files, but they are
static archives and do not churn. Don't chase it.

**FIXED 2026-08-14 ~18:28 — Eric removed `~/DEV` from Drive Preferences → "Folders from your

- `PRECONDITION_FAILED` 14 → **0**. `ProcessDownloadEvent` errors 11 → **0**.

- Google Drive CPU **64.6% → 0.0%**.
- **End-to-end: 5/5 genuine placeholders (blocks==0) fetched in 2–3s each**, where the same
  class of read previously stalled for minutes or indefinitely. This is the actual cure for

## A stalled run with no rsync child = an unanswered macOS access prompt (2026-09-03)

`daily-backup.ps1` gates both optional destinations on a bare `Test-Path` with **no timeout**:
`Test-Path $GDrive` (section 2a) and `Test-Path $SsdRoot` (section 2b). When macOS has a pending
TCC/removable-volume permission prompt for that path, the call blocks **forever** — and because 2a
runs before 2b, the SSD capture never happens and no receipt is written.

**The tell:** `pwsh` alive in `S`/`SN` state, **zero rsync children**, and the log frozen mid-run.
That is not a slow copy — a slow copy always shows an `rsync` process. `ps -axo pid,stat,comm` on
macOS marks I/O wait `U`, not `D`; a `D`-state grep finds nothing and proves nothing.

**The fix is the human, not the shell — look at the screen for a pending prompt FIRST.** On
2026-09-03 both `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*` and `/Volumes/CRASHBOX` were unresponsive to
a plain `ls`. The Drive half cleared after a quit/relaunch of Google Drive, **but Eric was
approving access prompts in that same window — the relaunch is unproven and may have done nothing.**
Do not treat killing Google Drive as the known fix. The SSD half cleared only when he approved the
prompt. **Do not force-unmount CRASHBOX** (exFAT, no journal) — ask first.

Probably (unverified): the Claude Code shell and the launchd/reconcile jobs are different TCC
principals, so this prompt should not recur for the scheduled runs — but it may fire once per new
app that launches the script.

**Never re-run without `pkill -f daily-backup.ps1` first.** A hung run is harmless, but several hung
runs unblock *together* the moment access is granted and race onto the SSD — the two-writer
corruption this whole system exists to prevent.

**Timing that matters:** reconcile replays the backup at 07:00 if no `OK` is logged for today, and
launchd fires at 09:00 regardless (see "Current state" above). A manual run finishing before 07:00
suppresses the replay; one finishing after 07:00 can collide with it.

Open gap, not yet fixed: neither `Test-Path` has a watchdog, unlike `Invoke-Rsync`
(`$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900`). Worth wrapping both.
